Kesklinn — Tallinn, Estonia

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 8 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

No concerns found day Average night

In detail

The centre, and with it the walled Old Town where essentially every visitor stays. It is beautiful and it is also, by the account of the people who live in it, a rough place at night. ERR reported in October 2024 that the few remaining long-term Old Town residents no longer consider it safe to live in: more than 500 offences in the first five months of that year, an 18-year-old stabbed in the Kanuti garden, public drinking, fights, and young people carrying large knives, with one community police officer saying the call figures do not reflect what is actually happening. Estonia's thefts hit a ten-year high in 2025 and Tallinn has an established professional pickpocketing problem, now working bar cloakrooms rather than pockets. Walk it freely by day; the small hours in the bar streets are the part being described.

Frequently asked questions

Is Kesklinn safe?

Wandroz currently rates Kesklinn in Tallinn as an area where the review found nothing traveller-relevant to report during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Tallinn at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Tallinn publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Kesklinn safe at night?

At night, Kesklinn is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Tallinn. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Kesklinn a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Kesklinn's day rating (an area where the review found nothing traveller-relevant to report) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Note that the Booking.com link on this page searches Tallinn, not Kesklinn specifically: Booking does not list this neighbourhood as a destination of its own, so check each property's address against the map above.

Not an official government crime feed — Kesklinn's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used).
